clue.text: Popular impression of opening-time?

definitions.note: playfully, the time when a life is just opening, its beginning

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fancy is a notion or vague impression

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about the public's idea of when the pub opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening-time' looks like pub hours, but it means the start of life; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyhood is the earliest stage of life, its opening period.

clue.text: Instructor doomed to take people on square

parts.note: in for it means bound to suffer, doomed
to man a post is to staff it with people
a T-square is a draughtsman's square, giving its letter

explanation.surface: A teacher fated to take a group of people onto a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets T after the other pieces in this down clue. The definition is loose: one who informs.
explanation.definitionFit: A source who tells or gives information acts as a teller of facts.

clue.text: Warning to leader of privateer from a nautical platform

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of the ball

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word heads it

explanation.surface: A warning shouted to a pirate captain from a ship's lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's top platform at the head of the foremast is a lookout station.

clue.text: Gothic home of Hugo's squatter?

parts.note: Victor Hugo's hunchback Quasimodo lived in a Paris Gothic cathedral; a squatter is jokingly a squat, hunched figure

explanation.walkthrough: 'squatter' suggests an illegal occupant, but means one of squat build: Quasimodo the hunchback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cathedral is the home of Victor Hugo's hunchbacked bell-ringer.

clue.text: Brewer's cart turning up in the area

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upward reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for carrying beer barrels

explanation.surface: A beer cart appears in the yard of the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed open space by a building is a patch of ground.

clue.text: Extinct ruminant or ox, you could say

indicators.note: signals that the clue words are to be spoken, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: the two words run together when spoken

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether a long-dead grazing beast was a different animal or an ox.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild ox of ancient Europe, ancestor of domestic cattle, died out in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Old druggist made a lot of money, varying each line

parts.note: a pot is a large sum, as in pots of money

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are altered in order

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A chemist of old got rich by charging a different amount for each product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges EACH into HECA.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, one who prepared and sold medicines was a pharmacist.

clue.text: Nurses set up society

parts.note: to rear is to raise or set upright

explanation.surface: Nurses founding a professional society.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean bring up or tend a child or animal while it grows.

clue.text: One tries to make a purchase, even when on the rocks

definitions.text: One tries to make a purchase, even when on the rocks

parts.words: One tries to make a purchase, even when on the rocks
parts.note: a purchase is a firm grip or foothold, which a mountaineer seeks on a rock face; on the rocks also means broke

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shopper who is broke, but 'purchase' is a hold and 'on the rocks' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer scaling a crag constantly looks for handholds.

clue.text: Undressed kid won over, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: persuaded, influenced

explanation.surface: A child without clothes was persuaded, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undressed kid' looks like a naked child but means kid leather with an unpolished, napped finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather, often kidskin, with a napped unglazed finish is described as undressed.

clue.text: Leading rook held in hand

indicators.note: says the letter for rook is gripped inside the word for hand

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player keeps a leading rook clutched in their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first is being in front, at the head of the field.

clue.text: For hairdo, men disguised this red dye

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are concealed by being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Men colour their hair red to disguise themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges the letters of HAIRDO MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synthetic fluorescent dye giving a red or pink colour.

clue.text: Row in park is unpleasant

definitions.meaning: the first part of the name of ... Row, a riding track in Hyde Park, London

explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the famous horse-riding track in London's Hyde Park; the word that goes with 'Row' in its name is the answer. 'Row' is not a quarrel or a line here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something putrid or nasty is disagreeable; the word also completes the name of a London park track.

clue.text: Vestment for church, blue as ordered

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A church orders a blue garment for its clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges BLUE AS into ASUBLE; the surface's 'ordered' looks like a purchase, not a reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: This sleeveless outer garment is worn by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Bar fittings to keep stock in?

definitions.text: Bar fittings to keep stock in?

parts.words: Bar fittings to keep stock in
parts.note: a set of bars set in a road over a pit, to stop farm animals straying

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub's shelving for drinks; 'stock' is livestock and the 'bar' fittings are metal rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A road grating that farm animals will not cross keeps livestock in a field.

clue.text: Good exam result for the brightest star

definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation is designated by the first Greek letter

explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter names a top mark and the leading star of a constellation.

clue.text: Claret's an adaptation of blood

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks something, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A wine label claims the claret is a reworking of something bloody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation' rearranges CLARETS AN; claret is red wine and also old slang for blood, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherited through one's lineage or family line comes by blood.

clue.text: Cooks joint to make tender, perhaps

parts.note: steams is a way of cooking
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Someone steams a cut of meat to make it tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an adjective for meat; it is a small boat serving a larger vessel, an example of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a vessel, and a vessel driven by steam is one kind.

clue.text: Runner for tacking on the beach?

definitions.text: Runner for tacking on the beach?

parts.words: Runner for tacking on the beach
parts.note: a wheeled sail vehicle that runs over sand and changes direction by tacking like a boat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests a jogger and 'tacking' sewing; here they are a wheeled sailing craft and its zigzag course.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled sailing vehicle is raced along flat sands.

clue.text: One bringing anguish to soldiers trapped in twin peaks

indicators.note: the soldiers are caught between the two hilltops
the word for peak is taken twice over

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor
men are ordinary soldiers, other ranks

explanation.surface: A tormentor's victims are soldiers trapped between two mountain peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twin' doubles the peak word; 'trapped in' sets the soldiers between the copies. Tors are rocky hilltops, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A persecutor inflicts suffering and distress on others.

clue.text: Tear butter-paper?

parts.note: one that butts, as a ram does
a page is a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A command to rip the paper used for wrapping butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but a thing that butts; 'Tear' rhymes with 'bear', meaning rush about.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear around wildly is to go on a violent spree.

clue.text: Thomas Bruce, marbles champion

definitions.meaning: the 7th Earl's personal name, his title being an earldom
the earl who brought the Parthenon Marbles to Britain, which bear his name

explanation.walkthrough: The Parthenon sculptures in the British Museum are named after the earl who removed them from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The 7th Earl, born Thomas Bruce, took the Athenian sculptures now named for his earldom.

clue.text: Pieces of armour for Barking people?

definitions.meaning: the residue of melted tallow, formerly pressed into cakes as dog food, so fit for barkers

explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but the capital is a decoy: dogs are the 'barking people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shin plates of armour share a name with tallow scraps fed to dogs.

clue.text: For one of these terms, see variety …

definitions.text: For one of these terms, see variety

indicators.note: a variety of the letters, that is a mixed-up arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A cross-reference in a book, sending the reader to 'variety' and on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges TERMS SEE; the whole clue also describes an academic half-year term.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities divide the year into two halves, each a teaching period.

clue.text: Gentleman is a bishop, perhaps, out of work

indicators.note: a loose suggestion that the letters may be some other arrangement
the work is removed from the bishop word

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A bishop who has lost his job is still a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes OP from BISHOP, leaving BISH; 'perhaps' rearranges A BISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A respectful term of address for a European man in colonial India, like 'sir'.

clue.text: Paving-blocks for Brock's homes

definitions.meaning: squared stones used for road surfaces
Brock is the traditional name for a badger, whose burrows have this name

explanation.walkthrough: Brock is the folk name for the badger in British stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone road blocks share a name with badgers' underground dens.

clue.text: … in the old Empire?

parts.note: an archaic word, one found in old usage, meaning imperial rule or dominion

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this with 22: the answer is an old-fashioned form close in spelling to 'empire'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for sovereignty or an imperial domain.

clue.text: Tragedian getting on in part

indicators.note: only a portion of the word is used, the letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: A tragic actor who is growing old in a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on means growing old.

clue.text: Did it serve, for Dickens, as a matting wicket?

definitions.text: Did it serve, for Dickens, as a matting wicket?

parts.words: Did it serve, for Dickens, as a matting wicket
parts.note: Dickens wrote The Cricket on the Hearth; a cricket on a fireside mat imagined as a game played on a mat pitch

explanation.walkthrough: A matting wicket is a cricket pitch laid with matting; Dickens's insect cricket lived on the hearth, so its mat became the 'pitch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rug laid before a fireplace is where Dickens's chirping insect sat.

clue.text: Ruin of a number in pawn endlessly

indicators.note: the letters for 'a number' are placed inside the shortened pawn word
the last letter of the word for pawn is cut off

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone is ruined by an amount owed at the pawnshop that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims HOCK to HOC; 'in' puts A and V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread destruction or devastation is ruin.

clue.text: Poor-spirited sort, getting a smaller amount in retirement

definitions.note: adjective used of a person: the Beatitudes call the poor in spirit this

indicators.note: the smaller amount goes inside the word for retirement

parts.note: retiring for the night means going to bed
less is a smaller quantity

explanation.surface: A downcast person finds their pension smaller than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: From the Sermon on the Mount: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit'. 'Poor-spirited' looks like despondent but points to the Beatitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes say the meek and lowly in spirit are favoured by God.

clue.text: Place stake?

definitions.meaning: to put or set something down
money paid down as a pledge or bet

explanation.definitionFit: To put down is to place; money put down as security or a bet is a stake.
